en: Majjhima Nikāya 71:
The Discourse to Vaccha on the Threefold True Knowledge.
Thus have I heard—
At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Vesālī in the Great Wood, in the Gabled Hall.
Now on that occasion the wanderer Vacchagotta was residing at the Ekapuṇḍarīka Wanderers’ Park.
Then, in the morning, the Blessed One dressed, took his bowl and robe, and entered Vesālī for alms.
Then it occurred to the Blessed One:
"It is still too early to wander for alms in Vesālī;
what if I were to go to the Ekapuṇḍarīka park of the wanderers, where the wanderer Vacchagotta is?"
Then the Blessed One approached the wanderers’ park called Ekapuṇḍarīka, where the wanderer Vacchagotta was staying.
Seeing the Blessed One coming from afar, the wanderer Vacchagotta said this to him:
“Come, Bhante, let the Blessed One come.
Welcome, Bhante, to the Blessed One.
It has been a long time, Bhante, since the Blessed One made this occasion for coming here.”
"Venerable sir, let the Blessed One sit on this prepared seat.
The Blessed One sat down on the prepared seat.
Then the wanderer Vacchagotta, taking a certain low seat, sat down to one side.
As he was sitting to one side, the wanderer Vacchagotta said this to the Blessed One:
“Venerable sir, I have heard this:
‘The ascetic Gotama is all-knowing and all-seeing; he claims a knowledge and vision that is entirely exhaustive.’”
‘Whether walking, standing, sleeping, or waking, knowledge and vision are constantly and continuously present to me.
Venerable sir, as for those who say: ‘The ascetic Gotama is all-knowing and all-seeing;
he claims a knowledge and vision that is entirely without remainder, such that whether walking, standing, sleeping, or waking, knowledge and vision are constantly and continuously present to him’...”
"Are you present, venerable sir? "Venerable sir, do you speak as the Blessed One has spoken? Do you not misrepresent the Blessed One with what is false?
Do you explain in accordance with the Dhamma so that no legitimate ground for censure arises against you when you are challenged on your doctrine?"
“Vaccha, those who say of me: ‘The ascetic Gotama claims to be all-knowing and all-seeing, and that he professes a knowledge and vision without remainder, saying:
“Whether walking or standing, asleep or awake, knowledge and vision are constantly and continuously present to me,”’—they do not speak what has been said by me;
rather, they misrepresent me with what is untrue and false.”
“But how, venerable sir, should we answer so that we speak as one who speaks in accordance with what has been said by the Blessed One,
do not misrepresent the Blessed One with what is false, answer in conformity with the Dhamma,
and such that no legitimate criticism can be brought against us for falling into a position worthy of reproach?”
“Vaccha, if one were to declare, ‘The ascetic Gotama is a possessor of the threefold knowledge,’ one would be speaking exactly as I have spoken,
and would not misrepresent me with what is untrue; one would be declaring in accordance with the Dhamma,
and no legitimate objection could be found to warrant a point of reproach.”
For as long as I wish, Vaccha, I recollect my manifold past lives, that is to say:
one birth, two births... [as far as] thus with their aspects and particulars I recollect my manifold past lives.
For as long as I wish, Vaccha, with the divine eye, purified and surpassing that of humans, I see...
I see beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate...
I understand how beings fare according to their kamma.

For, Vaccha, through the destruction of the taints, I dwell having realized for myself with direct knowledge in this very life the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom, having entered upon them.
“Vaccha, if one were to declare, ‘The ascetic Gotama is one possessed of the threefold knowledge,’ one would be speaking exactly as I have spoken;
one would not misrepresent me with what is untrue; one would be explaining in accordance with the Dhamma;
and no legitimate criticism or objection could justly be brought against such a statement.”
When this was said, the wanderer Vacchagotta said this to the Blessed One:
"Is there, Master Gotama, any householder who, without having abandoned the fetters of a householder, makes an end of suffering with the breakup of the body?
"There is no such person, Vaccha, any householder who, without having abandoned the fetters of a householder, makes an end of suffering with the breakup of the body."
“But, Master Gotama, is there any householder who, without abandoning the fetter of household life, has, with the breakup of the body, gone to heaven?

“Not only one hundred, Vaccha, nor two hundred, nor three hundred, nor four hundred, nor five hundred; rather, there are even more householders who, without abandoning the fetter of household life, have, with the breakup of the body, gone to heaven.
“But, Master Gotama, is there any Ājīvaka who, with the breakup of the body, makes an end of suffering?”
“There is no Ājīvaka at all, Vaccha, who, with the breakup of the body, makes an end of suffering.
“But is there, Master Gotama, any Ājīvaka who, with the breakup of the body, goes to heaven?
“Vaccha, as far back as I recollect—ninety-one aeons ago—I do not recall any Ājīvaka going to heaven, except for one.”
“I am one who teaches action, Vaccha, one who teaches efficacy.
“If that is so, Master Gotama, then this sectarian position is empty, even of one who has gone to heaven.
“It is so, Vaccha; this sectarian position is empty, even of one who has gone to heaven.”
Thus the Blessed One spoke.
The wanderer Vacchagotta, being satisfied, rejoiced in the words of the Blessed One.
The First Discourse to Vacchagotta on the Threefold Knowledge is finished.
